title: Irkutsk: The Silence Isn’t an Answer
dek: Reports of a possible Russian lab incident have raised alarming questions. Here’s why I’m staying alert and keeping speculation in check.
note: An October 7 morning update on what we can responsibly conclude about the reported incident at Russia’s Anti-Plague Institute when reliable information is scarce: the unanswered questions around a lab worker’s death, why the first account never sat right with me, and how the Soviet record of bioweapons research and official secrecy informs the worry without proving anything about this case.

The honest takeaway is that we are in a wait-and-see period. The basic facts, the pathogen, and whether anything spread remain unresolved. I weigh both the reassuring and the worrying readings of the quiet, question whether a reported second death was duplicate reporting, and close with a separate concern about Trump’s comments on Russell Vought and the coming election.
